title: Building Generative Image & Video models at Scale - Sander Dieleman, Google DeepMind
talk_summary: A DeepMind research scientist walks through the full pipeline for training large diffusion models for image and video: data curation, learned latent representations, denoising/spectral intuition, transformer architectures, parallelism, guidance, distillation, and conditioning. It is a research/ML-training talk with almost no content about agent orchestration, LLM prompting, or software engineering workflows.

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of feeding raw high-dimensional data to the model, they train an autoencoder to produce a compact latent that keeps the same grid structure but is orders of magnitude smaller, because generic codecs obscure structure the model relies on.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we actually use compressed representations ... we actually learn our own compressor
takeaways.numbers: reduce tensor size by two orders of magnitude; 256x256 RGB -> 32x32 latent grid

takeaways.what_they_do: Diffusion sampling takes small steps toward a predicted target rather than jumping to the full prediction, and re-injects a little fresh noise each step to stop the model compounding its own mistakes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you keep feeding the network its own mistakes back ... you're going to go off the rails

takeaways.technique: Guidance-style contrast between conditioned and unconditioned predictions
takeaways.what_they_do: They run the model twice per step, once with the conditioning signal and once without, and amplify the difference to sharpen output toward the prompt at the cost of diversity.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you do need to do two model evaluations per step, but you get a huge increase in sort of sample quality
takeaways.numbers: 2x model evaluations per step for large quality gain
